title: Find the Winning Player in Coin Game
statement:
A pile holds `x` coins worth 75 each and `y` coins worth 10 each. Alice and Bob take turns, and Alice moves first. A move removes some coins from the pile whose values add up to exactly 115. The first player who cannot make such a move on their turn loses.

With each player always making their best possible move, return the winner's name: `"Alice"` or `"Bob"`.
notes:
## Intuition

Only one handful of coins is worth 115: one 75-coin and four 10-coins. Without a 75-coin the total would be a multiple of 10, and two 75-coins already make 150. So every move removes exactly one 75-coin and four 10-coins, and neither player ever has a real choice: the game is forced, and "optimal play" changes nothing. It lasts until one kind of coin runs out, which is after `min(x, ⌊y / 4⌋)` moves. Alice makes moves 1, 3, 5, ..., so she wins exactly when that number is odd. (A brute force could search the game tree over the remaining coins, trying every combination worth 115, and reach the same verdict.)

## Approach

1. `bigCoinMoves = x`: each move uses one 75-coin.
2. `smallCoinMoves = ⌊y / 4⌋`: each move uses four 10-coins.
3. `moves` is the smaller of the two: the game stops when either kind runs out.
4. Return `"Alice"` when `moves` is odd and `"Bob"` when it is even.

## Example 1, step by step

`x = 2`, `y = 7`: `bigCoinMoves = 2` and `smallCoinMoves = ⌊7 / 4⌋ = 1`, so `moves = 1`. Alice takes 75 + 4 · 10; one 75-coin and three 10-coins are left, which cannot make 115, so Bob is stuck. One move is odd, and the answer is `"Alice"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): a division, a minimum and a parity test.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Not rounding `y / 4` down: three leftover 10-coins cannot pay for a move.
- Zero moves is even: with `x = 1`, `y = 3` Alice cannot move at all, so Bob wins.
- Simulating a game with choices: 115 can be paid in only one way, so there is nothing to search.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bigCoinMoves` | moves the 75-coins allow (one per move) |
| `smallCoinMoves` | moves the 10-coins allow (four per move) |
| `moves` | how many moves the game lasts |

narration.2: 115 can only be paid as 75 + 4 × 10, so every move uses exactly one 75-coin: they last x moves.
narration.3: Every move also uses four 10-coins, so they last ⌊y / 4⌋ moves.
narration.4: The game stops as soon as either kind of coin runs out.
narration.5: Alice makes the odd-numbered moves; is the last move hers?
narration.6: Yes: Bob faces a pile with no move left and loses.
narration.8: An even number of moves (possibly zero) leaves Alice without a move, so Bob wins.
